LESSON: LISTENING FOR GIST

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.9: Listening for Gist

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Listening for Gist. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you pick out the main ideas from a listening text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify vocabulary related to the theme in listening texts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LISTENING FOR GIST
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Listening for Gist helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LISTENING FOR GIST
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify vocabulary related to the theme in listening texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify vocabulary related to the theme in listening texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify vocabulary related to the theme in listening texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for Gist”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify vocabulary related to the theme in listening texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Listening for Gist is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Listening for Gist”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify vocabulary related to the theme in listening texts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Listening for Gist to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify vocabulary related to the theme in listening texts.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Listening for Gist from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Listening for Gist: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Listening for Gist?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you pick out the main ideas from a listening text?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Listening for Gist means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify vocabulary related to the theme in listening texts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
